subject: Urgent: Aurelia - Hosted API tail latency spike during long-window inference
messages:
From: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@aureliahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Perez <james.perez@aureliahealth.com>, Aurelia SRE <sre@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 22:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact - sudden latency & errors on long requests

Ben —

We're seeing a large increase in p95/p99 on the hosted API for requests that include full patient histories (~16k tokens). The spike began ~21:00 PDT and has caused timeouts for several critical flows (triage summary generation). Error rate climbed to ~6% and p99 is hitting 7s+ (normal p99 ~800ms). We've attached a small sample payload and logs.

This is high-severity for us — we need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can route us away from whatever is affected.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Torres
Director of Product, Aurelia Health

Subject: Re: Production impact - sudden latency & errors on long requests

Elaine —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating internally right away. Short answers: we see a correlated spike in p95/p99 for large-context requests in the hosted-us-east pool starting ~20:50 PDT. We're opening an incident and will follow up with an action plan in the next 20–30 minutes.

Immediate asks for your team (if possible):
- Can you confirm whether those payloads used the 32k window flag or were capped at 16k?
- If you have a non-prod API key that reproduces the issue we can use to test routing changes without affecting production.

I'm adding Marissa (CS lead) and Dylan (SRE) to drive coordination. Grace — I'm going to loop you in for exec comms if this is high-impact for the account.

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 22:56:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Incident 8492 - initial triage notes

Incident summary:
- Alert: spike in p95/p99 latency + increased 5xx rate for hosted-us-east pool handling long-window inference.
- First signal: 2027-07-20T20:50:12Z. Peak error rate ~6.2% at 2027-07-20T21:08Z.
- Affected requests: payloads with ~12k–20k token contexts; specifically requests that pin the KV cache across multi-turn evals.

Initial findings:
- A scheduler regression in the continuous-batching allocator caused some large requests to be scheduled on nodes with fragmented KV cache state, leading to repeated KV reloads (observed 3–5x extra disk I/O on those requests).
- One kernel fallback path is being triggered more frequently for the quantized 16k model variant on a subset of machines (hosted-us-east-b group).

Immediate mitigations applied (22:45 PDT):
1) Emergency routing rule: divert confirmed Aurelia traffic to hosted-us-east-a (different node group) and to a smaller-context-compatible model variant.
2) Disabled a recent scheduling change in the allocator for long-window slices.
3) Increased soft timeouts to avoid client-visible 5xxs while we stabilize.

Next steps:
- Re-run targeted replay of sample requests (using aur-sample-16k) to measure p95/p99 improvements.
- If routing doesn't fully restore, apply temporary per-tenant throttling for >12k token requests and offer a fallback smaller-context summarization that reconstructs history server-side.

I'll continue updates in 15' or sooner if we have a rollback.

—Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: svc_logs_20270720_2200-0200.zip)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@aureliahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 23:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact - sudden latency & errors on long requests

Elaine —

Quick update: Dylan applied the routing change and we're seeing a measurable drop in p99 for the replayed samples (from ~7.2s to ~1.1s median on the diverted node group). There are still outlier cases at ~3–4s for some 16k requests — likely related to the kernel fallback.

What we're proposing for the next 24 hours:
- Short term (now to 6h): keep diverted routing + enable prefix caching for your tenant for repeated patient-history prefixes. This should cut repeated KV loads.
- Short‑to‑mid term (6–72h): schedule a controlled rollback of the allocator change across hosted-us-east-b and push a targeted kernel patch to reduce fallback frequency for the quantized 16k variant.
- Customer-facing: we'll throttle >20k token requests by default and surface a clear 429 with a recommended smaller-context path and an automated rehydration helper.

We can set a customer call in the next 30 minutes to walk through mitigations and get sign-off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Operational commitments from Redwood in next 24 hours:

- Patch kernel fallback and rollback the allocator tweak (targeted rollout with canary).
- Provide a pointer-by-pointer mitigation playbook and a one-hour follow-up status update at 11:30 PDT tomorrow.
- We will propose a credit against next invoice for SLA disruption — draft attached.

If you prefer, we can move to a dedicated lane (short-term reserved capacity) while we finish the patch; we'll include cost/ETA in the follow-up.
